create.name: Richmond Zen
create.bio:
Richmond Zen is a lay-led Soto Zen sangha in Richmond, Virginia, practising in the line of Shunryu Suzuki and meeting in the zendo of Ekoji Buddhist Sangha on Grove Avenue. An independent non-profit and a member of the Branching Streams network, it is guided by Josho Pat Phelan Roshi, abbess of Chapel Hill Zen Center, who visits regularly to give talks and individual practice guidance. Its head priest, Eden Kevin Heffernan, has practised Zen for more than three decades, led the group as a lay leader from 1999, was ordained in 2018 and trained at Tassajara; he is also a campus minister for Buddhist students at a local university.

The sangha sits together four times a week: Sunday mornings with walking meditation, chanting and Dharma study, Wednesday evenings, and early Tuesday and Friday mornings. Newcomers can join an orientation with meditation instruction twice a month, and on the first Sunday of each month a zazenkai offers a half-day or full day of sitting, oryoki meals and work practice. A monthly Zoom class on the Bodhisattva precepts returns in 2027, seasonal practice intensives and outdoor sittings by the James River deepen the year, and the group runs entirely on donations.

courses.title: Weekly Zazen Schedule
courses.description: Regular group sitting at the Ekoji zendo: Sunday mornings with two periods of zazen, walking meditation, chanting and Dharma study; Wednesday evenings with two periods and chanting; and short early-morning sittings on Tuesdays and Fridays.

courses.title: Newcomer Orientation and Meditation Instruction
courses.description: An introduction for first-time visitors, held twice a month, covering a sustainable sitting posture, attention to the breath, working with distracting thoughts and the forms used in the zendo. Sign up by email with the head priest.

courses.title: Zazenkai
courses.description: A monthly meditation intensive on the first Sunday, offered as a half day or a full day: sitting and walking meditation, chant services, oryoki meals and work practice. Everyone is welcome to join any part of the schedule; register by email.

courses.title: Precepts Study Class
courses.description: A Zoom class on the second Monday evening of each month exploring ethical conduct in Buddhism and the Sixteen Bodhisattva Precepts as handed down by Dogen, with a reading list including talks by the guiding teacher. The class resumes in January 2027 and is open to all.

free_resources.title: How to Practice Zazen (illustrated instructions)
free_resources.description: An illustrated PDF guide to Zen meditation, recommended to newcomers before their first visit, with a companion sheet on alternative sitting postures on the centre's resources page.

free_resources.title: Richmond Zen Chant Book
free_resources.description: The sangha's chant book used at services, free to download for home practice.
